parole.significato: a kayak; a long, narrow, decked boat propelled with a double-bladed paddle, originally an Inuit skin-on-frame hunting c…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Greenlandic qajaq (“kayak”), from Proto-Inuit *qayaq (“boat, kayak; build a kayak”), from Proto-Eskimo *qayaʀ (“boat, kayak”). Compare the parallel borrowings Norwegian Nynorsk kajakk, Danish kajak, Swedish kajak, German Kajak and English kayak.

parole.significato: pingo; a usually conical mound of earth or other loose material with a core of ice, occurring in regions of permafrost
parole.testo: Borrowed from Greenlandic pingu (“tussock, small hill, hillock”), from Proto-Inuit *piŋu (“mound, dune, hillock, swelling”), ultimately from Proto-Eskimo *pǝŋu (“hill, swelling”). parole.significato: a birdskin jacket; a traditional Inuit jacket or shirt made from bird skins, traditionally worn with the feathers or do…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Greenlandic timmiaq (“birdskin jacket”), from Proto-Inuit *tǝŋmi(r)a- (“bird, small bird”), from Proto-Eskimo *tǝʁmira- (“bird, goose”). Compare the parallel borrowing Danish timiak.

parole.significato: an umiak; a large, open traditional Inuit boat with a wooden or bone frame traditionally covered with animal skins, use…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Greenlandic umiaq (“umiak, traditional open skin boat”), from Proto-Inuit *umia- (“large skin boat”), from Proto-Eskimo *umi(r)a- (“large skin boat”). Compare the parallel borrowings Norwegian Nynorsk umiak, Danish umiak and English umiak.
